clue.text: It contains fuel for the smoke generator

definitions.text: It contains fuel for the smoke generator

parts.words: It contains fuel for the smoke generator
parts.note: the smoke generator sounds like a machine making a smokescreen, but it is a pipe, and the fuel is the shag or flake a smoker carries for it

explanation.surface: A technical description of a fuel tank feeding a smoke machine.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'smoke generator' is a pipe; its fuel is loose leaf, kept in a small pocket-sized bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe smoker keeps loose leaf in a small pouch, the container of the pipe's fuel.

explanation.surface: An instruction to make up an outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn out goods is to produce or manufacture them; a turnout is also a person's dress or equipage.

explanation.surface: Someone baffled to discover the Muse of history taking a break.
explanation.walkthrough: Clio is one of the nine Muses; read whimsically, the answer is to 'be mused', to be a Muse at rest rather than at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Bemused means bewildered or confused; the second reading splits it as being a Muse.

definitions.note: the byname given to the English king Edward, who built Westminster Abbey

parts.note: to come clean is to own up, to confess

explanation.surface: An ultimatum: admit everything or identify Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward the Confessor was the saintly Anglo-Saxon king of England before 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: King Edward of England was known by the epithet 'the Confessor' for his piety.

explanation.surface: A horseman narrowly leading a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse carrying 'one up' has a single rider aboard; being one up means having a narrow lead.

parts.note: the nursery-rhyme character is drawn as an egg, so his figure before he tumbled off the wall was of that shape; 'the Fall' teases a biblical reading

explanation.surface: A theological gloss on the nursery-rhyme character's state before the Fall of Man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figuratively' here means 'in figure', that is, in shape: Humpty-Dumpty was an egg until he broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Oviform means shaped like an egg, which is the shape of the nursery-rhyme figure.

parts.note: the TUC, Britain's Trades Union Congress; reading the answer as an instruction turns those three letters round

explanation.surface: Staff cuts within a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as wordplay says take TUC (the Trades Union Congress, the British workers' organisation) back, giving the clue's words; 'in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutback is a cut in spending or staff, a reduction.

clue.text: Jack is seen here with sailor Tom, full of vitality

parts.note: Tom Bowling is the dead sailor of Charles Dibdin's famous sea song
green means fresh, young and vigorous

explanation.surface: A sailor called Jack in the company of a lively shipmate Tom.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack looks like a sailor beside Tom, but it is the small white ball aimed at in the game of bowls.
explanation.definitionFit: The jack is the target ball in bowls, which is played on a smooth lawn laid out for the game.

clue.text: The propeller is out of the water

definitions.text: The propeller is out of the water

parts.words: The propeller is out of the water
parts.note: the propeller is not a ship's screw but a person who drives a boat with blades that rise out of the water at each stroke

explanation.surface: A boat's screw raised clear of the sea, perhaps for repair.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower propels a boat by hand, and lifts the blades clear of the water between strokes.

clue.text: Reformed the citadel of the law

indicators.note: reformed means made over in a new shape, so these letters are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A fortress refashioned to house the courts.
explanation.definitionFit: Edictal means relating to an edict, a decree having the force of law.

clue.text: Small funeral vessel has damaged the jolly Royal Yacht!

indicators.note: damaged suggests something knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the cheerful royal yacht has been wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges RM (a 'jolly' is a Royal Marine) with ROYALYACHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A lachrymatory was a small bottle, once said to hold mourners' tears, found in ancient tombs.

parts.note: two words for the act of using one's eyes: to look and to see
two words for the act of using one's eyes: to look and to see

explanation.surface: A quick inspection that makes the examiner see two of everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double vision' supplies two seeing words, one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A look-see is informal for a quick inspection or survey.

explanation.surface: A remark that an apartment lacks romance.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosaic means dull and lifeless, and also matter-of-fact rather than poetic or romantic.

parts.note: something absent is not there, giving the word not
Ed is a boy's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A teacher recorded the lad as away from school.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a register being marked; the answer reads as 'not Ed', the boy missing.
explanation.definitionFit: To be noted is to be observed or remarked on, as a marked feature is.

clue.text: Like Dr Manette's, his work is done at last

definitions.text: Like Dr Manette's, his work is done at last

parts.words: Like Dr Manette's, his work is done at last
parts.note: Dr Manette in A Tale of Two Cities took up cobbling in the Bastille; a last is the foot-shaped block such a craftsman works on

explanation.surface: A man whose labours, like those of Dickens's Dr Manette, are finally complete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' seems to mean finally, but a last is the wooden foot model on which footwear is made.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler or bootmaker works on a last, as Dickens's Dr Manette did while imprisoned.

clue.text: Former pupil joins sit-in with fixed idea

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil of a school
a session is a sitting, a period of sitting in for business

explanation.surface: An ex-schoolboy takes part in a protest occupation, driven by a single idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sit-in' suggests a protest but here means a sitting; OB, old boy, is British for a former pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsession is an idea that preoccupies the mind and will not leave it.

explanation.surface: Kindnesses bestowed by star performers.
explanation.definitionFit: Good turns are favours or kind acts; headline performers give excellent acts on stage.

indicators.note: possibly signals a possible version of the letters, a rearrangement of them

explanation.surface: A complaint that something might be exceedingly boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the extreme' reads as an intensifier; the definition is 'the extreme', with 'in' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The outside is the utmost limit, as in 'at the outside', the most that can be expected.

parts.note: not inns or hotels but the ends of railway or bus lines, where journeys finish

explanation.surface: A description of wayside inns.
explanation.definitionFit: Ends of transport routes, where trains and buses halt, are their final stations.

parts.note: singular looks like strange, but means the one-item grammatical form of a plural word for facts

explanation.surface: Some odd intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singular' looks like 'peculiar'; it is the grammatical number of the Latin word whose plural is data.
explanation.definitionFit: A single fact or item of facts and figures is the singular of data.

explanation.surface: A footballer moving clubs without a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver is to set free or rescue, and also to hand over or convey goods.

clue.text: Group of three in charge of tong

definitions.note: an adjective: relating to a Chinese secret society, the kind called a triad

parts.note: a triad is a set of three

explanation.surface: A trio heading a Chinese secret society.
explanation.walkthrough: A tong is a Chinese secret society, also called a triad; the definition is adjectival, 'of tong'.
explanation.definitionFit: Triadic describes things pertaining to a triad, the Chinese criminal society known also as a tong.

clue.text: Entrance for the enclosure in the tenth rally

indicators.note: the answer is enclosed within the words that follow, sitting across them

explanation.surface: Gate-entry to the paddock during the tenth motor rally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' is the verb, to delight; the answer sits enclosed in 'tENTH RALly'.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthral is to captivate or delight someone, which is what entrance means as a verb.

definitions.text: The Grape that can with ____ absolute

parts.words: The Grape that can with ____ absolute
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from FitzGerald's Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam: wine can refute the seventy-two jarring sects with this reasoning

explanation.surface: A line from FitzGerald's Rubaiyat with a word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The full lines are 'The Grape that can with ____ absolute / The Two-and-Seventy jarring Sects confute'.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute reasoning or argument is what FitzGerald credits wine with, in the missing word of the quotation.

clue.text: Player to sit out after a game of cards

indicators.note: after places the rearranged letters following the card game

parts.note: solo, or solo whist, is a card game

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters of sit are put out of place

explanation.surface: A card player told to sit out the next hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sit out' looks like a phrase but 'out' rearranges SIT to IST; 'after' puts it behind SOLO; 'to' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A soloist is a performer who plays alone, a solo player.

clue.text: Pinning down is part of boxing

explanation.surface: A wrestling hold is one aspect of fighting with gloves.
explanation.definitionFit: Nailing means fixing or establishing firmly; it is also part of making a crate, fastening the planks with nails.

clue.text: He bursts in, having driven a different way

indicators.note: taking the letters a different way means rearranging them

explanation.surface: A man who crashes in after taking an unusual route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driven' looks like the motoring verb, but DRIVEN A are the letters rearranged by 'a different way'; 'having' links.
explanation.definitionFit: An invader is someone who forces his way into a place.

parts.note: the church season's name is split to show SUN in its middle, so it is literally sun-centred

explanation.surface: A stargazer's word for the Christian feast of Pentecost.
explanation.walkthrough: Whit-SUN-tide has the sun at its centre, like the Copernican model of the solar system.
explanation.definitionFit: Heliocentric means having the sun as the centre, as in Copernicus's model of the planets.
